title: Show your screen with Display Capture
summary: Add a Display Capture source so the preview shows your monitor.

steps.say: Find the Sources panel, second from the left in the bottom row of OBS. Say done when you see it.
hints: The Sources panel sits right of Scenes and left of the Audio Mixer.
If the panels are missing, open the Docks menu at the top and choose Reset Docks.
steps.why: Everything that appears in your video is added as a source in this panel.

steps.say: Click the plus button at the bottom left of the Sources panel.

checks.prompt: Is a pop-up list of source types, including Display Capture, now open?

hints: The plus sign is a small icon under the list of sources, at its left edge.
You can also right-click empty space inside the Sources panel and choose Add.
steps.why: The plus button lists every kind of source OBS can capture.

steps.say: Choose Display Capture from the list.
hints: Display Capture is near the top of the list, with a monitor icon.
Window Capture is a different item; pick the one that says Display.
steps.why: Display Capture records a whole monitor, which suits tutorials and screen recordings.

steps.say: Keep Create new selected and click OK to name the source.

checks.prompt: Is a properties window for Display Capture open, with a Display dropdown?

hints: You can type a clearer name such as Main screen before clicking OK.
Press Enter to confirm the dialog.
steps.why: Naming sources helps you tell them apart once a scene has several.

steps.say: In the Display dropdown, pick the monitor you want to show, then click OK.

checks.prompt: Does the large preview now show a picture of a computer desktop that was not there before?

hints: Displays are listed by number and resolution; your main screen is usually the first.
If the preview stays black on a laptop, try the other Capture Method in the same window.
steps.why: With several monitors, OBS needs to know which one to record.

steps.say: Look at the preview. You should see your screen inside OBS. Say done when it shows.

checks.prompt: Does the OBS preview show a copy of the desktop, often repeating into itself like a hall of mirrors?

hints: A picture that repeats inside itself is normal; it is OBS showing its own window.
If the source is listed but the preview is empty, check that its eye icon in the Sources panel is on.
steps.why: The preview is exactly what your recording will contain.
